artists.biography:
The Selecter are a 2 Tone ska revival band from Coventry, England, formed in mid 1979.
The Selecter featured a racially diverse line-up. Their lyrics featured themes connected to politics Reinforcing the songs of Neol Davies were the voice and rude girl style of Pauline Black and the rhythms of Desmond Brown on the Hammond organ. The band's name is based on the term "selector", which is a Jamaican word for disc jockey. The band were one of the most successful ska bands of the 2 Tone era, notching up a handful of hit singles in the British charts.
The Selecter reformed in 1991 and vocalist, Black, continued to perform and release music under The Selecter name until 2006. Some confusion emerged over two competing lineups for the Selecter in 2011, between that featuring Davies and that featuring Black and Arthur 'Gaps' Hendrickson, In June 2011 Black applied for, and won, The Selecter trademark and the right to use the name herself.

perplexity.description:
Too Much Pressure, released in February 1980 on Two-Tone Records, is the debut album by British ska revival band The Selecter. The album showcases a blend of original compositions and covers of classic ska and reggae tracks, following a template similar to that of The Specials' debut album. It captures the band's energetic live sound, recorded shortly after their formation in 1979, and features politically charged lyrics addressing social issues such as racism, economic hardship, and societal division, notably through songs like the title track and "They Make Me Mad".

Musically, Too Much Pressure is rooted in the 2 Tone ska style, combining upbeat rhythms with sharp, socially conscious vocals led by Pauline Black. The album was produced by Errol Ross and recorded at Horizon Studios, reflecting the tight musicianship of a band that had quickly gelled on stage. It includes notable singles such as "Three Minute Hero" and "Missing Words," both of which charted in the UK top 25. Commercially, the album was successful, reaching number 5 on the UK Albums Chart and remaining there for thirteen weeks, marking the band's highest chart position to date.

Critically, Too Much Pressure was well received upon release, earning five-star reviews for its vibrant sound and incisive commentary. Reviewers praised the clarity and distinctiveness of each instrument and vocal part, as well as the band's ability to blend diverse influences into a cohesive whole. The album helped solidify The Selecter's place in the late 1970s/early 1980s ska revival movement and remains a significant work in the genre's history.
